intent: Adjust geometry to improve controller effectiveness by narrowing wheel_track from 0.15 to 0.14 to enhance turning agility without losing much stability, and reducing sensor_size from 0.016 to 0.012 to sharpen line edge detection and reduce sensor overlap. These changes aim to provide the controller with clearer, more precise sensor data and better physical agility, helping reduce off-track events and steering oscillations seen in previous races.
rationale: Integrator feedback and race telemetry show that while the current geometry with 7 sensors, sensor_size 0.016, and wheel_track 0.15 provides good line detection resolution and turning stability, the robot still goes off track early due to controller compensating for insufficient steering precision and oscillations. The integrator suggested trying a slightly narrower wheel_track (0.14) to allow quicker turning response without sacrificing too much stability, and a smaller sensor_size (0.012) to reduce sensor overlap and improve edge detection sharpness. These geometry changes should help the controller by balancing stability and agility and improving sensor signal clarity, enabling better steering control and reducing oscillations. Other geometry parameters remain unchanged to maintain the stable baseline. I request measurements of completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, and line_loss_events to evaluate the impact of these geometry adjustments in the next race.
